P04-001.grounds: Both primaries hit this row; most items verify, one OL support is REFUTED on the bytes and one LF scope claim needs narrowing, so refine. LF ITEM 1 (internal rival unnamed), upheld with a scope correction: the span does absorb a third-person presentative opening its own sub-scene, הִנֵּ֤ה יוֹם יְהוָה֙ בָּ֔א (oshb:Isa.13.9, byte tier), “Behold, the day of Yahweh comes, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger; to make the land a desolation, and to destroy its sinners out of it.” (web:Isa.13.9), and no rival naming it appears anywhere in the row, while the sibling row treating a structurally parallel presentative at web:Isa.10.33 both discloses it as a live internal-seam candidate and argues why it does not cut. The correction: those two rows belong to DIFFERENT writer parts, so this is a cross-part practice inconsistency rather than one writer treating the same construction two ways within one stretch — real, but a narrower charge than 'this same writing stretch' implies. LF ITEM 2 (internal count mismatch), upheld cleanly: the rejected-alternative calls a stand-alone header row here 'a fourth ... alongside Isa.1.1 and Isa.2.1'. The book carries exactly three headers of this class (MT 1:1, 2:1, 13:1), so setting this one apart would make a THIRD such row, not a fourth; the sentence names two precedents and then miscounts its own addition. OL ITEM 1 (the stated ground does not discriminate), upheld and STRENGTHENED by my own re-derivation: the relative clause אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.13.1, byte tier) is byte-identical not only to MT 2:1's but to MT 1:1's as well — all three headers carry the same accented clause (sweep: 3 verses) — so 'grammatically fused to the content it opens' cannot separate this header from EITHER named precedent. OL's proposed discriminator checks out on the bytes: this header binds its target to the burden-noun in construct, מַשָּׂ֖א בָּבֶ֑ל (oshb:Isa.13.1, byte tier), while the other attaches its target with a preposition after the patronymic, בֶּן אָמ֑וֹץ עַל יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Isa.2.1, byte tier). I also checked OL's digit against its object and it is RIGHT where it could easily have been wrong: the verb-then-prophet adjacency stands at exactly 2 verses (MT 2:1 and 13:1), because MT 1:1 places the name BEFORE the verb — a different object from the 3-verse relative clause. OL ITEM 2, REFUTED AS STATED: the ketiv/qere site at MT 13:16 is real, staged as the doubled pair וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם תשגלנה תִּשָּׁכַֽבְנָה (oshb:Isa.13.16, byte tier for the spliced run), and this row is one of the 8 undisclosed cases corpus-wide against 35 disclosed. But the support offered for it is false about this row: there IS no 'English clause quoted for that boundary' — the row quotes no English at web:Isa.13.16 at all, its only English quotation being the header at web:Isa.13.1. The site survives as a practice deviation; the reason given for it does not. OL ITEM 3 (first person already running), upheld: אֲנִ֥י צִוֵּ֖יתִי (oshb:Isa.13.3, byte tier) and וּפָקַדְתִּ֤י (oshb:Isa.13.11, byte tier) are divine first person inside the span and a bare presentative already stands at MT 13:9, so calling the next verse 'a distinct divine first-person Behold onset' names two features already present; the byte feature actually distinctive at the seam is the first-person SUFFIX on the presentative. Field boundary_rationale: delete the governance narration attached to the header decision and state the ground by content alone. Field boundary_rationale: correct the back-seam description so the distinctive feature named is the first-person suffix on the presentative, not 'behold' and not first person as such, disclosing that divine first person already runs at web:Isa.13.3 and web:Isa.13.11 and that a bare presentative already stands at web:Isa.13.9. P04-002.challenge_claim: The onset is byte-sound, verse-initial and genuinely distinctive, but a catchword attested in exactly two verses of the book straddles this row's front seam undisclosed, and the near-time predication brackets the whole burden across the same cut.
P04-002.grounds: Byte-re-derived; the challenge verifies on every object it names and is upheld, with one tier clarification. The onset is sound and the challenge says so: הִנְנִ֛י (oshb:Isa.13.17, byte tier) is the first token of its verse, and the quoted run הִנְנִ֛י מֵעִ֥יר עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם אֶת מָדָ֑י (oshb:Isa.13.17, byte tier) matches the source bytes; the first-person-suffixed presentative reaches 14 verses book-wide at skeleton tier and this is its only site in the oracle, so it is genuinely distinct from the bare presentative at MT 13:9. FRONT-SEAM CATCHWORD, upheld: the shatter-root stands at exactly 2 verses in this book (sweep: 2 verses, MT 13:16 and 13:18), and I confirm each form is a hapax on its own — וְעֹלְלֵיהֶ֥ם יְרֻטְּשׁ֖וּ (oshb:Isa.13.16, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse) on the far side of the cut and וּקְשָׁת֖וֹת נְעָרִ֣ים תְּרַטַּ֑שְׁנָה (oshb:Isa.13.18, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse) on this side — so the two are not byte-identical to each other and the recurrence is skeleton tier, which the challenge names honestly. TIER CLARIFICATION: the cross-seam rule as written triggers on a BYTE-true device straddling a seam, so this recurrence carries under the tier-disclosure standard instead — a skeleton-tier cohesion signal counts only with its tier named, which it is. On that footing the finding stands: a two-site catchword falling on both sides of an oracle-internal join is owed a disclosure, and neither side of the seam gives one. NEAR-TIME BRACKET, upheld: כִּ֥י קָר֖וֹב (oshb:Isa.13.6, byte tier) opens the day-of-Yahweh call inside the preceding unit and וְקָר֤וֹב לָבוֹא֙ (oshb:Isa.13.22, byte tier) closes this unit's last line; I re-swept that skeleton and confirm 8 verses with the list matching exactly, so this row's closing line answers a verse sitting inside the preceding unit and brackets the whole burden across the internal cut. GOOD DISCIPLINE, credited: the challenge correctly excludes the homograph pair across the same cut as a near-miss rather than counting it as a catchword, and correctly quotes the named instrument rather than sweeping a bare skeleton that is a short-token trap. VERIFIES: the back seam opens כִּי֩ יְרַחֵ֨ם יְהוָ֜ה (oshb:Isa.14.1, byte tier), a causal clause with a new addressee; no petuchah or setumah and no ketiv/qere note inside MT 13:17-13:22, the next mark being a setumah at MT 14:2 outside the span — all correctly left unclaimed; and retaining the header-bounded value without a fresh header is right. Severity low is correct: the cut holds and only its cohesion disclosure is missing.
P04-002.remedy: WORK ORDER (author wave). Field device_notes: disclose the two-site shatter-root catchword falling on both sides of this row's front seam — web:Isa.13.16 on the far side and web:Isa.13.18 on this side — quoting both forms, naming the tier (skeleton, since the two forms are not byte-identical to each other) and the digit (2 verses), with the argued reason the cut still stands across it. Field device_notes: disclose that the near-time predication brackets the whole Babylon burden across this internal join, from web:Isa.13.6 inside the preceding unit to this unit's closing line at web:Isa.13.22, with the splices, the tier and the digit (8 verses at skeleton tier). Field boundary_evidence_refs: add web:Isa.13.6 and web:Isa.13.18 once they are argued. The paired disclosure on the other side of this seam is one edit with the sibling row's — a seam-pair cure, not two independent ones. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: every cohesion device straddling an oracle-internal join is disclosed with its tier and digit on BOTH sides of the seam, and a skeleton-tier recurrence is never described as byte-true; the mark and ref checks stay clean. Disclosure order only — no boundary change is proposed or authorised.

P04-003.challenge_claim: The row's opening seam rests on a verse-initial subordinating particle whose byte function argues continuity backward across that very cut, and its closing seam carries an undisclosed servant-root catchword hook.
P04-003.grounds: Kernel real at both seams; the framing overstates. FRONT SEAM: כִּי֩ is token 1 of 18 at oshb:Isa.14.1 (byte tier, re-spliced and re-collated), and a verse-initial subordinating particle does bind its clause to what precedes, so citing that run as the row's opening driver without disclosing the backward dependence is a genuine gap. But 'the one positive Hebrew signal standing at the cut' is byte-false: the same verse carries the participant shift the row actually names -- יְרַחֵ֨ם יְהוָ֜ה אֶֽת יַעֲקֹ֗ב וּבָחַ֥ר עוֹד֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.14.1, byte tier) brings Jacob and Israel in as the objects of the two verbs, against the Babylon-palace subjects closing oshb:Isa.13.22 -- and explicit participant/addressee shift is a tier-1 driver class under the owner addendum, so the cut is not carried by the particle alone. The challenge's own device-site sweep over Isa.14.1-Isa.16.12 re-derives exactly (tier-1: burden-word 2 verses, Isa.14.28 non-initial and Isa.15.1 verse-initial; postpositive signature 2 verses, Isa.14.22 and Isa.14.23; woe-family 1 non-initial verse, Isa.16.4; zero messenger-formula, zero divine-speech-verb adjacency, zero Holy-One-of-Israel title). BACK SEAM: upheld -- oshb:Isa.14.2 carries לַעֲבָדִ֖ים and oshb:Isa.14.3 carries הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה and also עֻבַּד (all byte tier), both verses standing in the eved-family inventory, so a root-level echo does cross the row's own close undisclosed; it is NOT a byte-true repeated device (three distinct tokens on one root: plural noun, abstract noun, verb), so the cross-seam cohesion rule is not triggered at its own terms and the challenge's 'catchword hook' wording runs ahead of the tier. Two limbs fail outright. The parashah limb corrects nothing: the row already reads the tier-3 setumah at Isa.14.2 as corroborating the frame that opens at Isa.14.3, which IS the correct after-the-verse orientation, single witness, SAMEKH never conflated with PE. And the challenge's own oshb:Isa.13.22 quote is EMPTY where it is labelled byte tier, so that limb ships no bytes at all.
P04-003.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed. (1) boundary_rationale: add one clause disclosing that the cited opening run begins with a subordinating particle whose clause is syntactically dependent on the preceding announcement, and that the seam is carried by the participant shift into Jacob and Israel rather than by the particle. (2) device_notes: add one sentence disclosing the eved-family root echo across Isa.14.2|Isa.14.3, tier named as root/skeleton level and explicitly NOT a byte-true repeated device, naming the three distinct objects (לַעֲבָדִ֖ים plural noun at oshb:Isa.14.2 against הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה abstract noun and עֻבַּד verb at oshb:Isa.14.3) so the servant referent classes are not blended into one digit. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the front-seam disclosure must name a tier-1 signal other than the particle, and every Hebrew form added must re-collate at byte tier against its own cited ref with no identity claim asserted between the three root-sharing tokens.

P04-005.challenge_claim: The bracket conclusion survives the bytes, but the run quoted as the unit's closing evidence is not verse-final, and the signature count-object is mis-specified.
P04-005.grounds: Both limbs re-derive exactly from the bytes. QUOTE PARITY: oshb:Isa.14.23 has 11 tokens; the row's quoted closing run וְטֵֽאטֵאתִ֨יהָ֙ בְּמַטְאֲטֵ֣א הַשְׁמֵ֔ד is tokens 6-8 (byte tier), and the verse actually ends נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת at tokens 9-11 (byte tier). The row's word 'ending' is therefore byte-false, and the quote stops three tokens short of the very device its bracket argument rests on. COUNT-OBJECT: the couplet carries THREE signature tokens over two verses, not two -- נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת at oshb:Isa.14.22 tokens 3-5, then verse-final in that same verse נְאֻם יְהוָֽה at tokens 12-13 (bare tetragrammaton, NO hosts-title), and verse-final נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת at oshb:Isa.14.23 (all byte tier). The two verse-final stacks are skeleton-equal in their first two tokens and byte-DISTINCT (accents differ), and the hosts-title stands only at oshb:Isa.14.23, so the row's 'repeated neum-YHWH-Tsevaot signature' wording and its repeated-hosts-title signal key leave the third token and its different stack unnamed -- against the divine-name discipline that a citation names the exact stack it counts. The device is postpositive rather than an onset at both sites, so the couplet is signature-CLOSED at both ends. The tier-3 PE at Isa.14.23 is correctly typed, correctly oriented (seg after the verse) and single-witness disclosed, never a driver.
P04-005.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed -- the bracket conclusion survives. (1) boundary_rationale: re-splice the oshb:Isa.14.23 closing evidence so the quoted run reaches the verse end and carries נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת itself rather than stopping at וְטֵֽאטֵאתִ֨יהָ֙ בְּמַטְאֲטֵ֣א הַשְׁמֵ֔ד. (2) boundary_rationale + device_notes: replace 'The repeated neum-YHWH-Tsevaot signature' with wording that names three signature tokens over two verses and states that the hosts-title stands at two of the three, the third being the bare-tetragrammaton stack verse-final at oshb:Isa.14.22. (3) observed_substrate_signals: correct the repeated-title key so the repeated object is the signature formula, with the title stack named per site. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the re-spliced closing run must re-collate at byte tier against oshb:Isa.14.23 AND terminate at that verse's final token, and every signature digit in the row must name its exact title stack and its unit.

P04-007.challenge_claim: The mid-verse placement of the burden-word is byte-true, but the directional construal the row builds its boundary on is unsupported by the bytes and contradicted by the row's own bounds; and the row's signal key merges petuchah and setumah into one label, against the rule that the two mark types are never conflated.
P04-007.grounds: FIRST LIMB UPHELD. הַמַּשָּׂ֥א הַזֶּֽה closes oshb:Isa.14.28 as tokens 6-7 of that verse's 7 (byte tier), so the non-initial placement is byte-true and the site is correctly held apart from the verse-initial header class (tier-1 sweep: 10 verse-initial header verses, unit = verses; this verse is inventoried as a non-initial site). The defect is the stated direction: the row calls the burden-word 'a backward-pointing reference to the burden it dates', and no byte supports the reversal. The same noun-plus-demonstrative construction הַמָּשָׁ֥ל הַזֶּ֛ה stands at oshb:Isa.14.4 (byte tier) immediately before the speech it introduces -- cataphoric -- and this row's own span places the dated burden AFTER the notice, so the stated construal argues for a seam the row did not draw. SECOND LIMB REFINED, NOT UPHELD: no conflation occurs. The row's prose types each mark at its own verse -- petuchah at Isa.14.27, setumah at Isa.14.32 -- and both validate against the mark inventory at tier-3, single witness, with the after-the-verse orientation correct in both cases (the PE closes Isa.14.27 so it precedes this span; the SAMEKH closes Isa.14.32 so it closes it). Nothing is read as the wrong type and nothing is counted as one object. The residue is only that ONE signal key names two mark classes in a single entry -- a field-hygiene wobble under the dotted signal-key contract, not a PE/SAMEKH conflation -- and carrying it at the same weight as the construal defect overstates it.
P04-007.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed. (1) boundary_rationale and device_notes: replace 'backward-pointing reference to the burden it dates' with the byte-supported reading -- a mid-verse header reference inside the regnal dating frame, pointing forward to the burden this row's own span carries -- leaving the non-initial-placement finding and the retained unit_type disclosure unchanged. (2) observed_substrate_signals: split the compound parashah key into two entries, one per mark class. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the corrected construal must be consistent with the row's own span direction and must not assert a direction the demonstrative parallel at oshb:Isa.14.4 contradicts; each parashah key must name exactly one mark class, each still validating against the inventory under the claimed type at its own MT key, single witness.

P04-008.challenge_claim: The row's confidence value exceeds the governing cap for a span that covers an entire chapter.
P04-008.grounds: Upheld on arithmetic the row cannot survive. The span is Isa.15.1-Isa.15.9; chapter 15 carries exactly 9 verses in BOTH witnesses (identity numbering here -- neither offset zone touches ch 15), so the row covers the whole chapter start to finish with no remainder at either end, and its recorded confidence is 'high' while the campaign's chapter-fallback rule caps a whole-chapter span at medium_low. The cap is a live band, not a nominal one: all four bands are in use across the frozen corpus (medium_low 40 rows, low 4). Everything the challenge concedes also verifies independently: מַשָּׂ֖א מוֹאָ֑ב stands verse-initial at oshb:Isa.15.1 (byte tier) and is one of the ten verse-initial header sites (tier-1 sweep: 10 verses); the mid-verse paragraph opening immediately after the header is tier-4 layout and the row uses the folded verse text rather than inheriting a break from it; the tier-3 setumah at Isa.14.32 is correctly typed, correctly oriented and single-witness disclosed. NOT NAMED BY EITHER LENS, and it makes this more than a one-field edit: dropping to medium_low pulls the row into the low-band sidecar regime, so the cure carries mirroring and frontier-queue obligations the row does not currently satisfy. The other lens supported this row without registering the cap at all.
P04-008.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed -- the span itself re-derives as sound. (1) confidence: set to medium_low. (2) Because that band is now in force, mirror the row into all three sidecars with the FULL schemas (why_low_confidence, concern_type, possible_downstream_risk, suggested_reviewer, proposed_atlas_action, promotion authorities, review states), with bespoke non-boilerplate uncertainty text keyed to this span rather than to the cap rule. (3) Add the frontier-queue row the low band requires, and revisit frontier_flag_considered rather than leaving it at its drafted value. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: no span equal to a full chapter may carry a confidence above medium_low anywhere in the batch, and every row at or below medium_low must resolve to a sidecar row in each of the three sidecars plus its frontier-queue entry.

P04-009.challenge_claim: OL: the row's own opening-seam driver sits inside an undisclosed ketiv/qere verse whose variant changes the addressee, and the span's woe-family token is left unverified. LF: the unit's own content is a plea for asylum closing on a Davidic-throne promise rather than judgment against the target nation, and this operative-category deviation from the retained label is not disclosed. DISTINCT defects, not one -- the first is a byte/disclosure failure inside the span's own evidence, the second a governance-schema omission -- and both uphold.
P04-009.grounds: OL LIMB ONE UPHELD AND STRENGTHENED. Four of the five imperatives the row names as its driver stand in oshb:Isa.16.3, a variant-note verse (1 note; the campaign's largest such inventory, single witness), staged as a DOUBLED token pair at the very head of that chain: הביאו unpointed (skeleton grade only, not quotation grade) beside הָבִ֤יאִי pointed (byte tier), the two differing exactly in addressee ending. The row discloses no variant note anywhere, and it argues from that verse. Stronger than either lens stated: the addressee does not merely alternate at that one pair -- it turns THREE times inside the row's own span. שִׁלְחוּ at oshb:Isa.16.1 (byte tier) is masculine plural; oshb:Isa.16.3 sets עֲשׂ֣וּ masculine plural against feminine-singular שִׁ֧יתִי at token 6 and סַתְּרִי֙ at token 11 and תְּגַלִּֽי at token 15 (all byte tier); oshb:Isa.16.4 addresses מוֹאָ֛ב with הֱוִי (byte tier), a masculine-singular imperative; and oshb:Isa.16.5 is third-person throughout. So 'continuing the appeal's own addressee' is contradicted by the bytes the row is built on, and the undifferentiated second person of the English witness cannot show it -- the continuity reading is translation-carried. OL LIMB TWO UPHELD AT LOWER WEIGHT: הֱוִי at oshb:Isa.16.4 is skeleton-identical to the book's woe particle but byte-distinct in its pointing -- hataf-segol and hiriq against the accented holam-pointed particle ה֗וֹי at oshb:Isa.17.12 and the same form at oshb:Isa.18.1 and oshb:Isa.55.1 (byte tier) -- an imperative of the verb 'to be', not a woe onset. It is the one woe-family token verse inside this span and the inventory itself flags this site for per-site verification, so a row arguing no internal seam across exactly that span owes the disclosure; nothing about the seam moves on it. LF LIMB UPHELD AND DISTINCT: the unit's own bytes carry no header, no woe cry, no divine-speech frame and no judgment announcement -- בְּאֹ֣הֶל דָּוִ֑ד at oshb:Isa.16.5 (byte tier) closes an asylum plea on a throne promise -- so the retained massa_oracle value is an operative-category deviation, and the operative-category law requires a one-sentence deviation disclosure in device_notes that this row lacks while two comparably-postured rows in the same cluster carry theirs. Tier-3 owes nothing here: no parashah seg falls in Isa.16.1-Isa.16.5, and that absence is never counterevidence.
P04-009.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed. (1) device_notes: add the variant-note disclosure at Isa.16.3 -- single witness, one note, the doubled pair named with הביאו labelled skeleton grade (unpointed in the extract) and הָבִ֤יאִי labelled byte tier -- and state that the two forms differ in addressee. (2) device_notes: rewrite the continuity clause so it no longer asserts a single continuous addressee; the retained cut may instead be argued from the absence of any frame onset between Isa.16.4 and Isa.16.5, with the span's addressee turns disclosed rather than smoothed. (3) device_notes: add the one-sentence operative-category deviation disclosure for the retained unit_type, in a formulation distinct from the ones already used by the neighbouring rows. (4) device_notes: add one clause verifying the woe-family token at Isa.16.4 per site as a form of the verb 'to be' and not a woe onset, naming the pointing difference from the particle. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS: the variant-note sentence must validate against the note inventory under the claimed type at the MT key with single-witness disclosure; every form-class label must re-derive from the pointed bytes at its own cited ref; and no continuity claim may survive that the span's own addressee turns contradict.

P04-010.challenge_claim: The row's only mark citation is oriented backwards: the seg it calls the unit's opening stands one verse later, inside the span, at exactly the interior seam the row denies.
P04-010.grounds: Upheld. The setumah is inventoried at Isa.16.6 and the seg stands AFTER that verse's words, so it marks Isa.16.6|Isa.16.7 -- interior to this row's span -- and not the row's opening seam at Isa.16.5|Isa.16.6, where the inventory records nothing at all (chapter 16 carries exactly two marks, Isa.16.6 and Isa.16.14). The error is local to this row: the same writer applies the after-the-verse reading correctly in four neighbouring rows, at Isa.14.2, Isa.14.23, Isa.14.27 and Isa.14.32. Type and disclosure are right (SAMEKH, tier-3, single witness, never conflated with PE, flagged non-driving), so the defect is the located role, not the citation. The consequence is substantive rather than cosmetic: the row's rejected alternative denies any seam between Isa.16.6 and Isa.16.12 while the seg it cites corroborates one at Isa.16.6|Isa.16.7, where לָכֵ֗ן stands verse-initial at oshb:Isa.16.7 (byte tier) after the report onset שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ גְאוֹן מוֹאָ֖ב opens oshb:Isa.16.6 (byte tier). ONE CORRECTION TO THE CHALLENGE'S WORDING, not to its finding: לָכֵ֗ן is a consequence particle binding back to what precedes, so calling it an 'onset' reads it more strongly than the same packet reads verse-initial כִּי֩ at oshb:Isa.14.1 on the front seam of another row in this cluster; the interior signal is real but it is a backward-binding discourse connector, and this tier-3 layer cannot drive a seam in either direction.
P04-010.remedy: Author work order, no boundary change proposed -- the tier-3 layer is not a driver and the span is not moved on this ground.
